text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Health authorities have called for growth in Vietnam's antibiotics industry, as drugs to tackle contagious disease and parasites now account for 30 percent of all medicine.
-- Vietnam's VP Bank was not hurt by the arrest on fraud charges of some of its high-ranking officials and clients last week, according to General Director, Huynh Buu Son
-- Investment from China and Hong Kong amounted to $2.5 billion by June 28, 1997, according to the Ministry of Planning and Investment.
-- Water levels on the Red River peaked on Thursday morning with the level measured in Hanoi at 11.09 metres (above danger mark 2).
-- Vietnam's National Assembly Chairman, Nong Duc Manh, has congratulated a visiting delegation from the Laotian National Assembly Office on the occasion of the admittance of Laos into ASEAN.

-- Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai has told staff at the Central Religious Committee to study harder in order to have better knowledge of religious matters, so that they can better understand the opinions and wishes of believers.
-- 99.45 percent of voters from 60 of Vietnam's 61 provinces took part in elections last Sunday for the tenth session of the National Assembly. Election results will be announced next Monday.
-- President Le Duc Anh has issued a letter of address to invalids and families of war martyrs on the occasion of the 50th anniversary of War Invalids and Martyrs' Day, on July 27.
-- The results of monetary policy in the first six months of 1997 have been poor and show unfavourable trends, said Deputy Governor of the Vietnam's State Bank Le Thi Ngot.
-- 33.1 percent of people living in mountainous areas and 36.8 percent of people living in the Mekong River Delta can not read or write.
